input.content:
A teacher showed you ONE example of a layout rule you cannot see. Work out the rule and commit it.
Your rule will be tested on many other inputs, not only this one. You may ask the teacher to show the true outcome on new inputs, but at most 3 times and every question has a cost. Decide for yourself whether you need to ask. When you are ready call commit with your rule, or call abstain if you cannot.

EXAMPLE (badge):
before = {"objects": [{"id": "card0", "x": 10, "y": 360, "w": 120, "h": 70}, {"id": "proto", "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 20, "h": 20}], "canvas": {"w": 1400, "h": 700}}
after = {"card0": {"x": 10, "y": 360, "w": 120, "h": 70}, "proto": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 20, "h": 20}, "badge": {"w": 20, "h": 20, "x": 102, "y": 368}}
('after' gives the geometry of every object once the hidden rule has been applied (new objects included).)

RULE GRAMMAR:
Write the rule as a few lines of text. Examples:
  let a = objects[0].w / 2
  clone objects[1] as badge at (objects[0].x + a, objects[0].y + 5)
  for o in objects with i { move o to (30 + i * 50, 200) }
Operators: + - * / ( ), comparisons, and/or/not, min(...), max(...), len(objects); fields x y w h; multiply and divide by constants only; numbers are integers or exact decimals.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask the teacher to show the true outcome of the hidden rule on a new input. At most 3 questions; each one costs. badge: card_widths has exactly one width; spacing: 2 to 5 widths. Widths are integers from 24 to 512.

tools.name: commit
tools.description: Commit your final rule, written as text in the rule grammar. It is final once it parses and evaluates; a rule that does not parse is returned to you with the error.
